cello.context: A cello standing on its endpin with its bow leaning beside it. Use it for orchestras, string lessons, classical music and chamber ensembles.

double-bass.context: A tall double bass with sloped shoulders, f-holes and a short endpin. Use it for jazz bands, orchestras and upright bass lessons.

violin-bow.context: A string instrument bow with the stick, the hair beneath it and the frog at the grip end. Use it for violin, viola or cello lessons, bowing technique and orchestra content.

lyre.context: An ancient lyre: two curved arms joined by a crossbar, strings running down to a sound box. Use it for ancient Greece, poetry, mythology and early music.

lute.context: A lute with a pear-shaped body, a rosette sound hole and a pegbox bent back at an angle. Use it for renaissance and medieval music, early music ensembles and fairs.

mandolin.context: A mandolin with a teardrop body, an oval sound hole and a flat headstock with tuners. Use it for bluegrass, folk, Italian music and string lessons.

banjo.context: A banjo with a round drum body, a long neck and a short fifth-string peg. Use it for bluegrass, country, folk and old-time music.

ukulele.context: A small ukulele with a figure-eight body, a round sound hole and four tuning pegs. Use it for Hawaiian music, beginner lessons and casual strumming.

bass-guitar.context: An electric bass guitar with an offset body, an extra-long neck and a headstock with tuners. Use it for bands, rock, funk and bass lessons.

double-neck-guitar.context: An electric guitar with two parallel necks rising from one body. Use it for rock concerts, guitar gear and stage performance.

resonator-guitar.context: An acoustic guitar with a large round metal resonator plate in place of a sound hole. Use it for blues, slide guitar, bluegrass and roots music.

balalaika.context: A balalaika with a triangular body, a small sound hole and a long neck. Use it for Russian folk music, cultural events and world music.

sitar.context: A sitar with a long wide neck, a large gourd at the bottom and a small gourd near the top. Use it for Indian classical music, raga and world music.

erhu.context: An erhu: a two-string fiddle with a small drum body, a tall thin neck, two pegs and a bow. Use it for Chinese music, orchestras and cultural events.

shamisen.context: A shamisen with a small square body, a long thin neck, tuning pegs and a fan-shaped plectrum. Use it for Japanese music, theatre and cultural content.

zither.context: A zither seen from above: a flat box with strings, a round sound hole and a fretboard strip. Use it for folk music, Alpine music and string instruments.

appalachian-dulcimer.context: An Appalachian dulcimer seen from above: a long narrow hourglass body with a fretboard down the centre. Use it for folk and old-time music.

morin-khuur.context: A morin khuur: a trapezoid body and a long neck topped by a carved horse head. Use it for Mongolian music, culture and throat singing performances.

ektara.context: An ektara: a gourd resonator with a split bamboo neck holding a single string. Use it for Bengali folk music, Baul songs and devotional music.

berimbau.context: A berimbau: a tall curved wooden bow with one wire string and a gourd resonator. Use it for capoeira, Brazilian music and percussion.

cigar-box-guitar.context: A cigar box guitar: a rectangular box body with a stick neck running through it. Use it for blues, DIY instruments and homemade music.

washtub-bass.context: A washtub bass: an upturned tub with a broom handle and a single string. Use it for jug bands, skiffle, folk and homemade instruments.

harpsichord.context: A harpsichord from above: an angular wing-shaped case with two keyboards at the front. Use it for baroque music, early music and keyboard history.

upright-piano.context: An upright piano: a tall cabinet with a keyboard across the middle and two pedals below. Use it for piano lessons, home music and practice rooms.

pipe-organ.context: A pipe organ: a symmetric row of pipes above a console with keyboards. Use it for churches, cathedrals, weddings and organ recitals.

harmonium.context: A harmonium: a box with a keyboard, a bellows flap at the back and a row of stop knobs. Use it for Indian devotional music, kirtan and qawwali.

concertina.context: A concertina with hexagonal end boxes and buttons, joined by pleated bellows. Use it for folk music, sea shanties and Irish sessions.

melodica.context: A melodica: a small keyboard body with a flexible tube and mouthpiece. Use it for school music, reggae and portable keyboard sounds.

synthesizer.context: A synthesizer: a wide keyboard with knobs and a small display above the keys. Use it for electronic music, music production and synth settings.

modular-synthesizer.context: A modular synthesizer: a rack of modules with knobs, jacks and a patch cable. Use it for electronic music, sound design and synth patching.

keytar.context: A keytar: a keyboard worn like a guitar, with keys along the body and a neck grip. Use it for 80s music, stage performance and synth pop.

theremin.context: A theremin: a small cabinet with an upright rod antenna and a side loop antenna, played without touch. Use it for electronic music, sci-fi sounds and experiments.

clarinet.context: A clarinet: a straight tube with a mouthpiece at the top, key holes and a small flared bell. Use it for bands, orchestras, jazz and woodwind lessons.

oboe.context: An oboe: a thin conical tube with keys, ending in a tiny double reed. Use it for orchestras, woodwind sections and music lessons.

bassoon.context: A bassoon: a tall wooden tube with a thin curved crook holding the reed. Use it for orchestras, woodwind sections and low wind parts.

recorder.context: A recorder: a straight pipe with a beak mouthpiece, a window and finger holes. Use it for school music lessons, early music and beginners.

pan-flute.context: A pan flute: a row of pipes bound together, stepping from long to short. Use it for Andean music, mythology and folk wind instruments.

ocarina.context: An ocarina: a rounded egg-shaped vessel flute with a mouthpiece and finger holes. Use it for folk music, game soundtracks and ceramic instruments.

harmonica.context: A harmonica: a long flat mouth organ with a row of square holes along its front. Use it for blues, folk, country and busking.

didgeridoo.context: A didgeridoo: a very long wooden tube that flares slightly at the far end. Use it for Aboriginal Australian music, drones and world music.

shakuhachi.context: A shakuhachi: an end-blown bamboo flute with nodes, a notched top and a rounded root end. Use it for Japanese music, Zen meditation and world music.

shawm.context: A shawm: a conical wooden pipe with a flared bell, a disc near the top and a short reed. Use it for medieval and renaissance music and historical fairs.

crumhorn.context: A crumhorn: a narrow capped wind pipe whose lower end curves up into a J hook. Use it for renaissance music and early music ensembles.

serpent-horn.context: A serpent: a bass wind instrument whose long tube winds in a snake-like S shape. Use it for early music, church bands and brass history.

sheng.context: A sheng: a cluster of bamboo pipes of different heights rising from a round cup. Use it for Chinese music, orchestras and free reed instruments.

hulusi.context: A hulusi: a gourd with a small bulb on top and three bamboo pipes coming out below. Use it for Chinese folk music and wind instruments.

trombone.context: A trombone: a long U-shaped slide, a mouthpiece and a forward-facing bell. Use it for jazz, big bands, orchestras and brass lessons.

french-horn.context: A French horn: circular coiled tubing with a wide flared bell. Use it for orchestras, brass sections and classical music.

tuba.context: A tuba: a large upright brass horn with coiled tubing, valves and a huge bell pointing up. Use it for brass bands, orchestras and oompah music.

sousaphone.context: A sousaphone: brass tubing wrapped in a big circle with a huge bell facing forward over the top. Use it for marching bands and parades.

bugle.context: A bugle: a simple brass horn with one loop of tubing, no valves and a flared bell. Use it for military calls, scouts and ceremonies.

hunting-horn.context: A hunting horn: brass tubing coiled into a single ring with a flared bell. Use it for hunting, heraldry and signal calls.

shofar.context: A shofar: a curved ram's horn with a narrow mouth end and a wide open end. Use it for Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur and Jewish ceremonies.

carnyx.context: A carnyx: a tall vertical war trumpet topped with an open-mouthed animal head. Use it for Celtic history, Iron Age culture and museums.

vuvuzela.context: A vuvuzela: a long straight plastic horn that widens steadily into a large bell. Use it for football fans, stadiums and loud celebrations.

air-horn.context: An air horn: an aerosol can with a trumpet horn on top giving out sound waves. Use it for alerts, parties, sports events and sound effects.

jaw-harp.context: A jaw harp: a small horseshoe-shaped metal frame with a springy tongue through it. Use it for folk music, twangy sounds and world music.

bullroarer.context: A bullroarer: a flat pointed wooden slat on a long cord, swung in a circle to make a roaring sound. Use it for ritual, history and world music.

drum-kit.context: A drum kit: a bass drum with two toms on top and a cymbal on a stand. Use it for bands, drummers, rock music and rehearsal rooms.

timpani.context: Timpani: a large kettle-shaped drum on legs with a mallet resting on the head. Use it for orchestras, percussion sections and dramatic music.

congas.context: Congas: two tall barrel-shaped hand drums standing side by side. Use them for Latin music, salsa, Afro-Cuban rhythms and percussion.

djembe.context: A djembe: a goblet-shaped hand drum with a wide head and rope lacing. Use it for West African music, drum circles and percussion classes.

tabla.context: A tabla: a pair of hand drums, one tall and narrow, one wide and round, each with a dark centre. Use it for Indian classical music and devotional songs.

cajon.context: A cajon: a wooden box drum in three-quarter view with a round sound hole on its side. Use it for acoustic sets, flamenco and unplugged percussion.

taiko.context: A taiko: a big studded barrel drum lying on a crossed wooden stand. Use it for Japanese festivals, drumming ensembles and performances.

frame-drum.context: A frame drum: a wide shallow round drum with a thin rim and a double-ended tipper stick. Use it for Irish music, Middle Eastern music and hand percussion.

talking-drum.context: A talking drum: an hourglass drum with cords running from head to head. Use it for West African music, storytelling and hand percussion.

steelpan.context: A steelpan: a shallow steel drum with dimpled note areas and two sticks. Use it for Caribbean music, calypso, carnival and steel bands.
